content.comment_body: I am trying to read an analog input connected to AI2. From the [product_name] interface, I can see the value changing. When I try to access it using the S7 protocol through both Kepware and Node read, I’m unable to retrieve the value. Kepware reports the error: 'Warning [company_name] TCP/IP Ethernet Channel1.[product_name] | Unable to read data from device. | Memory type = 'AI', block start = 2, block size = 2 (bytes), Reason = 'Device returned data access error'. Error code = 0X5.' Should remote reading of the AI2 value using S7 protocol be possible? If yes, what might be causing this issue? Thanks

I’m not familiar with Kepware specifically, but I recommend checking how the tag is set up and how it’s being utilized. If it’s configured for read-write access, try switching it to read-only. Alternatively, send the analog input to a network analog output and read the corresponding V-memory address, such as VW0, instead.
Hello, [user_name]. I found a helpful video on YouTube that assisted me earlier. Is this what you are looking for? [url]
Hello, you can read the value directly as a word from memory. For example, AI1 corresponds to memory word VW1032.
Thank you all for your support. Using memory address VM1034 resolved the problem.

analysis.insight_summary: The user sought to remotely access an analog input value from a [product_name] device using the S7 protocol via third-party applications, but encountered a device data access error. The problem was related to proper configuration and identifying the correct memory address for external read access, which ultimately solved the issue.
